main_text.l: dant : Nullis autem fidiculis aliud inde extorqueas, quam damnatum à se; si ultra premas, omnem sui damnationem, suæ mentis tantum & conscientiæ sententia fieri, omnino negamus sequelam. Nam à genere ad speciem alteram putida est consequentia, nec melior à re ad unum rei modum. Multis potest quis condemnare se ipsum, mente sua, ore suo, opere suo: de posterioribus modis aliquoties scriptura, de primo quantum memini nunquam. Confer Luc. xix. 21. Rom. ii, 1. Hinc Am-brosius, Hieronimus, Augustinus vocabulum Græcum exponunt, &, fortassis ante ipsos, Syrus interpres, ipse condemnat animam suam, uehou hajah naphs-hah: non condemnatur ab anima sua. Condemnat se suo facto, quod Ecclesiæ admonitionem spreverit: ore, quod verbis saltem amplectens omne Dei verbum, sic profiteatur veritates ex quibus convinci queat. En argumentum tuum Velthusi misere prostratum à Viro doctissimo jam ante quam tu id publicè tuum feceras. Sed quoniam quædam adhuc restant magni momenti adversus Wolzogium dicenda, hanc digressionem finio, postquam Wolzogio qualem virum Ortho-doxiæ tenacem dixerit imprudens, in memoriam re-vocavi.

page.notes: The woodcut below the text is a flower ornament (a rose with buds and leaves on a stem) and is not printed text. The printed page number is in old-style figures, read as 140. The text ends with "vocavi." and no catchword or signature is printed. Hyphens at line ends (Am-brosius, Ortho-doxiæ, re-vocavi, naphs-hah) are printed and kept. The Hebrew words are given in Latin transliteration as printed, not in Hebrew letters.
